explorations.title: Equally likely outcomes
explorations.instruction: Predict: if four outcomes are equally likely, what is H in bits? Then apply the preset, which sets n_outcomes and raw_weights.
explorations.observe: probs shows 0.25 for outcomes 1 through 4 and 0 elsewhere. contributions shows 0.5 bits for each active outcome. entropy H reads 2 bits.
explorations.why: Normalizing equal weights gives p_i = 1/4. Each contribution is -0.25 log2 0.25 = 0.5 bits, so four equal contributions sum to H = log2 4 = 2 bits. Equal probabilities maximize entropy for a fixed number of outcomes.

explorations.title: Certain outcome and zero probabilities
explorations.instruction: Predict: if outcome 1 has all the weight and outcomes 2 through 4 have zero weight, what is H? Then apply the preset, which sets n_outcomes and raw_weights.
explorations.observe: probs shows 1 for outcome 1 and 0 for outcomes 2 through 4. contributions shows 0 bits for every outcome. entropy H reads 0 bits.
explorations.why: Only outcome 1 can occur, so there is no uncertainty. A zero probability p_i = 0 makes c_i = 0 because the term -p_i log2 p_i is taken as 0, avoiding an undefined logarithm.
